answer: A practical defence is slow-thaw staking: every new identity must lock a deposit that melts like a glacier, releasable only in small tranches over weeks of honest participation. The deposit is the island a newcomer lives on — it cannot vote or claim rewards until its stake has demonstrably thawed through completed work and peer attestations. A sybil attacker faces the same frozen cost per copy, and dawn brings no shortcut: fresh copies start frozen again, so flooding the network with identities is expensive, slow, and self-defeating.
